reason: r22 adds the reacquire path. MHGU quests are split into numbered areas with a loading screen between them, so a hunt's gauge row, and with it the inserted mask, the 5-word object array and the 9-record draw block, dies and comes back at each transition (tester account of 2026-10-24, in the mhgu-understanding skill's rules and in work/modern-sharpness-gauge/PHASE2_RESEARCH.md; every run log agrees). The Forge skill's native GUI reference asks a plugin to restore its overrides while objects remain valid and to reacquire new objects without retaining stale pointers. r20/r21 detect a dead mask inside the mask's own enter handler, which cannot report the mask dying with its row: the handler stops being called (r20 read freed memory from t=630 with no links-lost line, and the plugin sat out the rest of the session). r22 adds insert::check_liveness to the draw walker's callback - the marker at mask+0x50, the mask's parent against the captured root, the root's child against the mask - and on failure counts the loss and runs the full re-arm (sampler controller, instance capture, row facts state, insertion addresses), so the next area's row is found, read and inserted like the first. The check reads only: the mask is reached through captured links, so a stale read drops addresses and never writes into freed memory. Three word reads per walker call while a mask is inserted. The clip geometry is r21's: insert::enter writes the authored pair, the position pair, the four rectangle words and the enable bit on every enter of the mask. r20 (NRO 5617ee906b0756af39676a6a3bdc4a4bf3b5fb55d5b1d18fed29978d552635fb, run on Eden 2026-10-24, user report: gauge disappearing) wrote it once per row and skipped the rest through a box cache, 206 of 206 probe lines at left == right; r18 (55340cfbec4fbdc176be57d3ac22356945c4f431f882eb784b362426a1e23330) wrote it from the walker's entry, 376 of 383 lines at left == right. The insertion itself has completed twice, with the cGUIInstance MT-allocated 5-word map, the draw block resized through the root's vtable slot 0x58 with main+0xa49b28's arithmetic, the class factory main+0xa4b6cc and the native linkers. Not approved for distribution; r12 and r13 were packaged and never run.
runtime_test: NOT RUN: r22 reacquires the gauge row after an area's loading screen, from the draw walker's callback. r21 (the every-frame clip write) and r22 are both unrun. r20 ran on Eden 2026-10-24 (installed bytes 5617ee906b0756af39676a6a3bdc4a4bf3b5fb55d5b1d18fed29978d552635fb): insertion completed, gauge missing, 206 of 206 probe lines at a zero-width box. r18 ran the same day with the same outcome. r17/r16/r15 ran clean; r14 ran once and failed as reported.

limitations: r4 has no runtime test; its lines, the 320-sample budget and the absence of any drawing change are static results.
r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r22 has not been run. Two completed insertions (r18, r20) each hid the gauge with a zero-width clip box; whether writing the box on every enter call (r21) leaves it non-zero has no runtime evidence, and the walker's reacquire check (r22) has never fired in a run
